title: Telemetry Decks — Sparse Viewport Chart Specs for Per-Model & Route Panels
creator: Aisha Park
description: Design a compact, horizontally-scrollable "deck" of per-model and per-route telemetry tiles ("sparse viewport") that surfaces latency, throughput, and token-economy signals at-a-glance and expands into detailed chart panels on hover/click. Goal: give platform users rapid triage and cost decisions for hundreds of routes without losing access to full distributional detail.
motivation: Large customers run dozens-to-hundreds of routes and model variants. Current large-panel views don’t scale for quick triage. We need a condensed deck UI that preserves key SLO signals (p50/p95/p99 latency, throughput, token-per-request, cost-per-1000 tokens) and enables fast drill-in patterns with consistent charting behavior across model and route contexts.
acceptance_criteria: Sparse deck layout shows 6 tiles per row on 1366px width with horizontal scroll. Each tile includes title (route/model), 3-line micro-summary (p50 / p95 / throughput), and a 120x48 sparkline.

Hover expands a focused panel in-place with full-size charts: latency distribution (violin + pX lines), throughput heat-grid, token waterfall, and cost delta bar. Expansion must be animated and dismissible.

Charts reuse a single spec for quantile lines and smoothing across deck and expanded panels; 1s, 1m and 1h aggregation windows available. Defaults: 1m aggregation with 5-minute smoothing for sparklines.
Tooltips include exact timestamp, numeric value, aggregation window, and request sample count. For latency distributions, tooltip shows sample median and sample size.
Conforms to accessibility color palette (WCAG AA) for severity overlays; red/amber/green thresholds are configurable per-project and exposed via the Console rollout settings.

Performance: rendering 200 tiles (server-side precomputed sparklines as SVG) must keep initial view paint under 600ms on a modern laptop in the staging environment. Fallback to precomputed PNGs for very large lists.
Design tokens and chart styles exported to component library (stories + CSS variables) and matched to runtime-1.18 chart component props.
Design review with PM, Eng (runtime + console), and Observability flagged and approvals recorded in comments.
chart_specs: Micro sparkline (tile): size 120x48, stroke-width 2, single-line area fill optional (alpha 0.06). Data window = 1h with 1m aggr; smoothing = simple moving average (span 5). Color: neutral/blue for healthy routes, accent color for selection.

Latency panel: stacked chart showing violin (distribution) on left, quantile lines (p50,p95,p99) over time on right. Y-axis = latency ms, log-scale toggle available. Quantile line styles: p50 solid, p95 dashed, p99 dotted. Aggregation windows: 1s/1m/1h. Outlier capping: show raw outliers as scatter overlay when zoomed.

Throughput panel: heat-grid where X = time buckets (1m default), Y = shards/instances (when available) or empty row for single instance. Cell color = requests per second normalized. Hover tooltip shows RPS and percent of route traffic.
Token waterfall: stacked area chart broken into prompt_tokens / completion_tokens / system_tokens. Tooltip includes tokens-per-request and cost estimate per 1k tokens based on route pricing tier.
Cost delta bar: small multiples across recent rollout windows showing percent cost change vs baseline. Bars colored by direction and annotated with absolute $/hr number.
Correlation overlay: optional toggle to overlay latency and token-rate on shared time axis with dual Y-axis and correlation coefficient in header.
Drill-in time range controls: predefined ranges [15m, 1h, 6h, 24h, 7d] + custom range picker. When switching ranges, maintain smoothing proportional to range length to avoid misleading wiggles.
Export & link: every tile has 'Copy permalink' and 'Open in full console view' actions; permalink supports encoded time range + drift annotation.
Data fallbacks: when sample sizes < 30 in window, show 'insufficient samples' indicator and gray the violin with guidance tooltip explaining statistical limits.
tradeoffs_and_decisions: Decision: Use precomputed sparklines at the API layer for initial deck render to meet performance targets. Tradeoff: slightly stale view (up to 30s) vs faster paint. Engineering to add live streaming for expanded panel only.
Decision: Default smoothing for sparklines = SMA; alternative advanced smoothing (Loess) rejected due to cost on client-side for large lists.
Tradeoff: Violin charts show richer distribution but are heavier to render; will only render violins in expanded panels and use quantile bands in tiles.
Decision: Cost estimates in token waterfall are approximate and include a 'cost-uncertainty' badge. PM requested an eventual toggle to show exact billing model per-customer.
Exploration: Consider adaptive pagination (server-side) for orgs with >1000 routes; scope out in follow-up ticket.
implementation_notes: Front-end: deck component should be virtualized list with precomputed SVG sprites for sparklines; expanded panel uses canvas-based charting (Plotly/Canvas kit) to show violins and >500 points efficiently.
Backend: telemetry aggregation service must expose endpoints for sparklines (1m aggr) and full-series (1s/1m/1h); include sample counts and outlier buckets.
API contract: /telemetry/decks?org={id}&range={}&aggregate=1m -> returns [{route_id, title, sparkline_svg, p50, p95, rps, tokens_per_req, cost_estimate}].
Instrumentation: include 'last_sample_time' and 'series_quality' flags to guide UI fallbacks.
QA: create smoke-tests ensuring deck renders with 200 synthetic routes and expanded panel populates within SLAs. Include visual regression snapshots for healthy/unhealthy states.
